source_disposition_policy.purpose: Keep direct research use of an official online text separate from acceptance of a locally stored source artifact.
source_disposition_policy.external_reference_acceptance: A human-reviewed official page or document may be used within the publisher, identity, language, displayed date/version or cutoff, relevant content and caveats actually checked. Record the review date and a useful section/page locator when available; an exact retrieval timestamp or stored response bytes are not required for ordinary reference use. Do not claim content or legal effect beyond the reviewed scope.
source_disposition_policy.local_copy_acceptance: Requires exact raw response bytes, resolved URL, retrieval time, media type, byte length and SHA-256. Converted text may be accepted as a complete artifact or as explicitly bounded passages after semantic validation against the original; capture identity alone is not text acceptance.
source_disposition_policy.count_semantics: accepted_source_count and accepted_current_law_source_count count locally stored source artifacts. accepted_derived_text_count counts complete derived-text artifacts accepted as documents; accepted_derived_passage_count counts individually bounded passages accepted from derived text while the remaining conversion may stay a candidate. accepted_external_reference_count is tracked separately and does not count as a local copy. None of these counts establishes topic adequacy or country review completion.

source_acceptance_gates.required: Verify publisher, document identity, source role, and whether the record is primary, secondary, guidance, form, case-law, or discovery-only.

Prefer the latest usable government-published consolidation. If only a dated or otherwise limited government-published text is usable, record its date/cutoff and publisher caveat and use it within that scope. Check a specific later amendment, commencement, repeal, or dependency only when it may materially affect the question; do not reconstruct the full amendment history by default or claim currentness beyond the evidence.

For captured records, retain exact source bytes, final URL, retrieval time, MIME type, and matching SHA-256. A matching hash proves byte integrity against the local ledger, not publisher authenticity or legal correctness.

Validate substantive text, structure, pages and annexes against the captured original. A complete derived text and an individually bounded passage have separate acceptance states; a narrowly reviewed passage may be accepted without accepting the rest of its conversion. Replayability alone does not establish transcription accuracy.

source_acceptance_gates.applies_when: The source is guidance, a form page, or an operational route with linked attachments, submission channels, appointments, or service providers.
source_acceptance_gates.required: Review a linked form, checklist, submission route, appointment rule, or service provider only when the question or conclusion relies on it. Track a separate record when it is retained or needs its own review; build an exhaustive inventory only when making an exhaustive operational-coverage claim.
Record legal effect, instrument category, personal and territorial scope, and material EU/national references. Preserve historical wording and identify successors without silently rewriting it.

separate_gates.required: For each legal topic, map primary legislation, implementing rules, procedures, remedies, guidance, and relevant decisions, or explicitly record the gap. This is not a source-level acceptance test.
All material topics must be adequately covered and unresolved priority gaps explicitly dispositioned. Source acceptance and topic adequacy do not alone complete the country review.
Assess publisher reuse conditions before redistributing source captures or substantial derived text. Keep this separate from whether a source is reliable for internal research.

language_policy.national_legislation: Prefer a usable government-published consolidation. When the Gazette is fragmented, inaccessible, or not available as one usable text, use the closest government-published version, including an official translation or consolidation, and record its language, publisher label, date/cutoff, and caveats. Use a specific Gazette act to resolve a material later change, commencement, correction, repeal, or missing provision; do not capture every enactment and amendment or reconstruct the full chain by default. Check authentic Greek wording only when the legal question depends on that wording, and do not describe a translation as authentic Greek text.
language_policy.secondary_greek_texts: Greek-language CyLaw captures remain secondary mirrors; Greek language alone does not make them primary or prove currentness.
language_policy.guidance_and_forms: Use the closest relevant government-published language version and record its language, date/version, and visible limits. Review a linked form or attachment only when the research relies on it; a separate capture, record, or hash is for retained-copy or monitoring work. Do not require every language version or infer a counterpart that was not reviewed.
language_policy.eu_instruments: Use the relevant official EUR-Lex language version for the question and record its date/version. Compare or retain multiple languages only when the issue depends on wording differences or both representations are needed; check later status only when current legal effect matters.

states: A source may support a bounded research finding before it is accepted into this local corpus. External-reference and local-copy acceptance are independent decisions and may coexist. A source is accepted only for its declared role and temporal scope after applicable gates pass. Accepted sources do not prove topic adequacy; adequate topic coverage does not alone complete the country review. Passage-level acceptance is recorded separately from complete derived-text acceptance: a bounded excerpt can be accepted against the original while the remaining conversion stays unaccepted.
